caption: The Woolies shop costs me about R800 more than Checkers would. Is that a fair price for being tired?

slides.title:
How I'm clearing
R92 000 of debt
on R35 200 p/m
Living in Kempton Park
slides.body:
Female, 33
Single, no kids
Job: Court interpreter
Net salary: R35 200 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 1 bed in a complex, water, parking
slides.body: I moved here for the short drive to work. The rent is the price of not sitting in traffic.

slides.title: Debt payments
slides.includes: Store accounts R2 100, credit card R2 300, personal loan R3 000
slides.body: Total owing is R92 000. I ran the avalanche and snowball maths side by side and the gap was R6 100 in interest.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: I wanted the Polo. The Picanto is what I could stretch to, and it's fine.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Woolies food, because I'm tired when I shop
slides.body: Checkers would be R2 400. I know that. I still walk past it.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My mother's rent, my cousin's college fees
slides.body: I haven't missed a month. I've never once told my mother how much of my debt this explains.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol, car insurance, medical aid, phone, electricity, funeral policy, stokvel, Netflix
slides.body: The stokvel is R500. It pays out in December and I know exactly where that money goes.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R35 200. R1 200 is what is left to put towards the debt on top of the payments, if nothing breaks.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statements to Beyond Horizon and it listed my debts and showed the avalanche and snowball payoff side by side.

Total interest was the number I'd never seen written down.

No bank login needed.
